text:
incident-bot: PAGER: P1 - GPU capacity exhaustion in prod-us-west-2. Autoscaler failing to add GPU nodes. Queue growth observed for realtime-inference. Paging oncall-riley :rotating_light:

oncall-riley: ACK. joining. saw alerts for > 90% pending pods in inference-queue namespace.

infra-sam: I'm looking at the autoscaler logs now. early signs: ASG attach profile rate-limit + launch template mismatch retries.

eng-jin: Confirming customer impact: several customer queries are timing out with 504s, customers on Dedicated tier impacted. CS informing top 3 affected accounts.

custsuccess-luis: FYI I've DM'd the two account owners. No billing impact, but degraded svc. Need ETA.

oncall-riley: Quick triage: can we scale non-gpu workloads down and evict low-priority inference pods to reduce queue pressure?

platform-maya: We have node taint stuck on recent launchtemplate change: new LT doesn't include instanceProfile arn:aws:iam::123456:instance-profile/gpu-node-profile, so nodes spin up but fail kubelet join with error `Unauthorized`. autoscaler retries then hits API rate-limit on AttachRole.

infra-sam: reproducing logs:
```
2026-03-15T15:07:12Z autoscaler: attach-instance-profile failed: Rate exceeded (AttachRolePolicy)
2026-03-15T15:07:13Z asg: launched i-0abcde but instance profile missing -> node tainted NoSchedule: join-failed
2026-03-15T15:07:17Z kubernetes: node report: kubelet: denied node registration: missing instance profile
```

sre-olga: So nodes are created but never become schedulable. autoscaler thinks capacity didn't increase and keeps retrying -> ASG spike + queue growth.

deploy-bot: Deploy pipeline note: last LT change rolled 2h ago to bump AMI and add gpu-driver-init systemd unit.

eng-jin: Hypothesis: new LT missing IAM attachment and has new taint key mismatched from infra expectation. Need hotfix: either revert LT or manually attach instance profile and untaint nodes.

oncall-riley: Action plan (hot path):
1) Prevent further ASG launches to avoid runaway rate limits (set desired=0 / pause autoscaler)
2) Manually increase existing ASG capacity with known-good LT (if available) OR temporarily create a small CPU fallback pool and route non-critical inference to CPU nodes.
3) Evict low-priority pods and enable preemption for batch workloads.
4) Customer comms: custsuccess-luis to send interim update.

platform-maya: I'm going to pause the autoscaler by adding annotation `cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/scale-down-disabled: true` to the ASG controller and set ASG desired count = current to stop launches.

infra-sam: I'll attempt manual attach of the instance profile to the recently launched instances (if in Pending) and then remove the taint. If nodes are healthy we can resume. If not, roll back LT.

oncall-riley: Riley taking point on orchestration. Sam + Maya you're owners for infra and platform steps. Jin prepare rollback PR in case. Olga, monitor SLOs. Luis prepare customer note.

custsuccess-luis: Draft note: "We're investigating a capacity issue causing increased latency and intermittent timeouts for inference in us-west-2. We're working to restore capacity; next update in 20m."

infra-sam: Manual attach attempt results:
```
aws ec2 associate-iam-instance-profile --instance-id i-0abcde --iam-instance-profile Name=gpu-node-profile
Result: association initiated
```
Followed by node join attempts:
```
kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep i-0abcde
# still NotReady (kubelet error: kubeconfig token rejected)
```

platform-maya: There are also taints applied by kubelet: `node.kubernetes.io/unschedulable:NoSchedule` and a custom taint `redwood/gpu-init=failed:NoSchedule`. If we can clear `redwood/gpu-init` after manual fix, pods should schedule.

eng-jin: While sams doing attach, I'm spinning up a temporary small pool (t4g-like) to take lower-latency but non-GPU workloads so we can free the queue. Creating a fallback nodegroup with CPU instances and tainting them `redwood/slot=cpu-fallback:PreferNoSchedule` and adding a scheduling rule for low-priority inference.

oncall-riley: Good. Prioritize: 1) stop autoscaler churn 2) get at least 2 GPU nodes healthy 3) drain and move critical pods.

sre-olga: Monitoring: pending pods in inference-queue dropped from 720 -> 420 after we evicted batch workloads and spun up CPU fallback. 99th latency still high for GPU-bound queries.

infra-sam: Manual remediation update: instance i-0abcde is now Associated and kubelet logs show token refresh success, but the node has `redwood/gpu-init=failed:NoSchedule` installed by systemd unit because nvidia-driver init script errored due to missing driver artifact in AMI.

deploy-bot: Note: AMI build job #642 failed earlier with missing gpu-driver tarball upload to artifacts bucket. Possibly why LT change was applied without the driver.

eng-jin: Path forward:
- Short term: remove taint from the two fixed nodes to let them accept pods (will run post-checks to ensure driver present).
- Mid term: rollback to previous LT (AMI) or rebuild AMI with driver then re-deploy LT.

platform-maya: Removing taint on i-0abcde now: `kubectl taint nodes i-0abcde redwood/gpu-init:NoSchedule-`

oncall-riley: Doing a small scale test: move 3 critical inference pods to i-0abcde.

sre-olga: Observing pods scheduling and readiness checks passing. Latency for those moved pods back to normal. overall queue decreased to ~120 pending.

custsuccess-luis: Sent update to customers: "We've restored a portion of capacity and routed lower-priority traffic to CPU fallback. We expect further capacity restoration in ~40 minutes. Apologies for the disruption."

infra-sam: Next steps: rebuild AMI with driver artifact fixed and include correct instance profile in LT template. Also add guard in rollout pipeline to verify IAM instance profile presence during LT creation.

eng-jin: I'll open a PR with a preflight check in the deployment pipeline (validate: AMI contains /opt/nvidia-driver and LT has `IamInstanceProfile`).

platform-maya: Autoscaler currently paused. After we confirm 4 healthy GPU nodes with correct LT, we'll unpause and let CA scale back to target.

oncall-riley: Wrapping up: current impact reduced. Paging -> oncall handoff completed. I'll stay for next 30m while we watch. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: capacity partially restored. Postmortem created: link https://redwood.internal/incident/1768702468 (created by oncall-riley).

eng-jin: I'll attach logs and the deploy pipeline diff to the postmortem.

sre-olga: I'll run an eval against traffic replay to ensure no regressions before we resume full autoscaler.

custsuccess-luis: I'll follow up with impacted customers after final restore.

oncall-riley: Good job team. Closing active pager for now, moving to postmortem/cleanup.
